objects.name: residential ancillary physical construction system
objects.definition: The coordinated physical assemblies added for swimming pools, alpine doorways, deck and balcony wall attachment, domestic solid-fuel heating, bushfire-resistant construction and private bushfire shelters.
functions: Coordinate ancillary building objects
Keep distinct regulatory pathways visible
Provide hosts for drawable components without claiming automatic compliance

ncc_references.relationship: Coordinates physical objects associated with pools, heating appliances, alpine areas, bushfire construction and private bushfire shelters.

cad.pattern: Connected group of project-selected ancillary assemblies
cad.placement: At the dwelling, associated Class 10 structures and external site works
cad.opening: Access, ventilation, drainage and service openings remain explicit
cad.load: Mixed structural, water, fire, environmental and occupant actions

notes: This catalogue is an object map, not a substitute for jurisdiction-specific approval, licensed standards, engineering or manufacturer instructions.

objects.name: alpine external doorway assembly
objects.definition: An external doorway in an alpine building arranged so that accumulated snow or ice does not prevent the door from opening, using an inward-opening or sliding configuration and coordinated threshold construction.
functions: Preserve an operable external doorway in snow conditions
Provide an egress opening
Coordinate the door, threshold and surrounding weatherproofing

ncc_references.relationship: Requires the external doorway configuration to remain openable when snow or ice accumulates.

cad.pattern: Framed wall opening with inward-swinging or sliding door state
cad.placement: At an external wall serving an alpine building
cad.end: External landing or alpine access assembly
cad.opening: Door clear opening and movement envelope are modelled separately from snow-clearance constraints
cad.load: Door loads to frame and wall; weather actions to seals and sill

notes: The required door operation is a configuration choice, not a new material. Snow build-up and clear-space checks remain project constraints.

objects.name: alpine doorway raised threshold
objects.definition: A raised sill, plinth or step-forming base at an alpine external doorway that lifts the door opening and weathering interface above the adjacent external surface.
functions: Raise the doorway above likely snow and meltwater accumulation
Support the door sill
Form a durable weathering interface

cad.pattern: Continuous raised base across doorway
cad.placement: Below external door frame and sill
cad.opening: Door opening begins above the raised threshold
cad.load: Door and occupant edge loads to wall or floor support

notes: A raised threshold may conflict with step-free access; the selected project solution must resolve both requirements where applicable.

objects.name: alpine doorway OPEN INWARDS sign
objects.definition: A durable physical sign fixed to an alpine external door in a Class 1b building to tell occupants that the door opens inward.
functions: Communicate door operation during egress
Remain visible on the door
Reduce delay or confusion at the exit

ncc_references.relationship: Class 1b inward-opening external doors require the prescribed operational notice on the inside face.

cad.pattern: Single sign plate or applied legend
cad.placement: Inside face of nominated alpine external door
cad.opening: Does not obstruct glazing, hardware or door movement
cad.load: Negligible sign load to door leaf

notes: The exact lettering and placement must follow the adopted provision; the sign is retained as real installed hardware rather than a drawing annotation only.

objects.name: framed deck or balcony wall-attachment assembly
objects.definition: The waling plate, structural fasteners, joist support, wall interface, flashings and deck bracing that connect an eligible framed deck or balcony to an external wall.
functions: Support deck or balcony joists at the building wall
Transfer attachment forces into the wall structure
Control water entry where cladding is opened or penetrated
not_synonyms: engineered connection outside the Part 12.3 limits

ncc_references.relationship: Provides the limited Deemed-to-Satisfy wall-attachment construction represented by this assembly.

cad.pattern: Linear wall connection with repeated fasteners and joist supports
cad.placement: Along an eligible framed deck or balcony edge at the external wall
cad.start: Building wall framing or core-filled masonry
cad.opening: Cladding removal and flashing returns remain explicit
cad.load: Deck gravity and bracing actions transferred through waling plate and fasteners to wall structure

notes: Part 12.3 has important limitations. A tool must not offer this assembly outside its scope without an engineered alternative.

objects.name: timber deck waling plate
objects.definition: A horizontal structural timber member fixed to the external wall and used to support and connect the inner ends of deck or balcony joists.
functions: Provide a continuous joist support line
Distribute deck attachment forces to wall fasteners
Receive flashings and joist connectors

cad.pattern: Single or joined horizontal timber run
cad.placement: Against external wall structure at deck joist level
cad.start: Plate end with required fastener edge distance
cad.end: Plate end with required fastener edge distance
cad.opening: Fastener holes and joist-connector positions are explicit
cad.load: Joist reactions and in-plane actions to wall fasteners

notes: Section, grade, span limits and fastener spacing are attributes governed by the selected path, not fixed ontology defaults.

objects.name: cold-formed steel deck waling plate
objects.definition: A horizontal cold-formed steel channel fixed with its web against an eligible external wall and used as the waling plate for deck or balcony joists.
functions: Provide a steel joist support line
Distribute attachment forces to the wall frame
Receive joist connections and flashings

cad.pattern: Horizontal lipped-channel run with repeated wall bolts
cad.placement: Web against steel-framed external wall at deck joist level
cad.opening: Bolt holes and joist connections are explicit
cad.load: Joist reactions and in-plane actions through channel web and bolts to wall frame

notes: The NCC-prescribed designation is a constraint for that path; proprietary alternatives require their own evidence.

objects.name: waling-plate wall-fastener group
objects.definition: A repeated, set-out group of screws, bolts or anchors that fixes the waling plate through or behind cladding into the nominated structural wall member or core-filled masonry.
functions: Transfer shear and tension between waling plate and wall
Keep fasteners aligned with sound structural material
Make connection density and end zones model-checkable

cad.pattern: Repeated fastener instances along waling plate
cad.placement: Through waling plate into structural wall support
cad.opening: Drilled or formed holes remain explicit where needed
cad.load: Connection shear and tension to wall structure

notes: Fasteners must land in the required structural material, not mortar beds, incidental blocking or timber end grain.

objects.name: No. 14 partial-thread self-drilling waling screw
objects.definition: A No. 14 self-drilling screw with a partly unthreaded shank used in pairs to clamp a timber waling plate to eligible timber wall framing under the nominated attachment path.
functions: Clamp the timber waling plate to framing
Transfer connection shear and tension
Provide repeatable mechanical attachment

cad.pattern: Paired repeated fasteners
cad.placement: Through timber waling plate into eligible solid timber wall member
cad.opening: Pilot or drilled path represented when fabrication detail is needed
cad.load: Shear, withdrawal and clamp action across plate-to-frame interface

notes: The exact proprietary screw must match the required geometry, material and evidence; gauge alone is not enough.

objects.name: M12 waling-plate connection bolt
objects.definition: A nominal M12 structural bolt used with a large washer to connect a steel waling plate to eligible steel wall framing in the Housing Provisions attachment detail.
functions: Clamp steel sections together
Transfer connection actions through aligned holes
Provide an inspectable mechanical connection
materials: stainless steel or protected steel where required

cad.pattern: Paired bolts repeated along steel waling plate
cad.placement: Through waling web and eligible steel wall member
cad.end: Nut and washer or detailed receiving side
cad.opening: Aligned bolt holes through both steel members
cad.load: Shear, bearing and tension across bolted connection

notes: Strength grade and snug-tight designation remain explicit connection attributes.

objects.name: large-diameter waling-plate washer
objects.definition: A thick large-diameter steel washer placed under an M12 bolt or anchor head to spread its bearing force over the waling plate face.
functions: Spread fastener bearing
Protect the waling plate face
Provide the detailed bearing area at the connection

cad.pattern: One washer per nominated bolt or anchor head
cad.placement: Between fastener head and waling plate
cad.opening: Central fastener hole
cad.load: Fastener bearing spread into plate

notes: Washer dimensions belong to the selected connection detail rather than a generic hardware default.

objects.name: M12 chemical waling-plate anchor
objects.definition: An M12 threaded anchor rod bonded into a drilled hole with a compatible chemical anchoring system to fix a timber waling plate to eligible core-filled reinforced masonry.
functions: Anchor the waling plate to filled masonry
Transfer shear and tension through bonded embedment
Provide an alternative to a mechanical expansion anchor

cad.pattern: Repeated bonded anchors
cad.placement: Through timber waling plate into core-filled reinforced masonry
cad.start: Nut, washer and rod at plate face
cad.end: Bonded embedment in filled masonry core
cad.opening: Drilled anchor hole is explicit
cad.load: Shear and tension through rod, bond and masonry core

notes: Horizontal chemical anchoring needs a product specifically suitable for that orientation and substrate; the ontology does not infer capacity.

objects.name: M12 mechanical expansion waling-plate anchor
objects.definition: An M12 mechanical anchor that develops its fixing action by expansion or another mechanical mechanism inside eligible core-filled reinforced masonry.
functions: Anchor the waling plate to filled masonry
Transfer connection shear and tension
Provide a mechanically activated alternative to bonded anchoring

cad.pattern: Repeated mechanical anchors
cad.placement: Through timber waling plate into core-filled reinforced masonry
cad.start: Anchor head and washer at plate face
cad.end: Expansion or mechanical engagement in masonry core
cad.opening: Drilled anchor hole is explicit
cad.load: Shear and tension through anchor mechanism to masonry core

notes: The selected anchor needs the required working-load evidence in the actual substrate and edge condition.

objects.name: joist-to-waling support connector
objects.definition: A hanger, cleat, bracket or detailed direct connection that supports and fixes the inner end of a deck or balcony joist to the waling plate.
functions: Support the joist reaction
Restrain the joist at the wall edge
Transfer joist loads into the waling plate
materials: structural timber blocking and fasteners where detailed

cad.pattern: One connection at each supported joist
cad.placement: Between joist end and waling plate
cad.opening: Fastener holes and any drainage gap remain explicit
cad.load: Joist reaction and restraint actions to waling plate

notes: The exact joist connection is coordinated with wall-fastener positions so the fasteners do not collide or weaken the same small zone.

objects.name: waling-plate junction flashing assembly
objects.definition: The top, bottom and side flashings, laps, fixings and seals installed around a waling plate where external wall cladding has been removed or opened.
functions: Drain water back to the exterior
Protect exposed wall framing and cladding edges
Weather the waling-plate penetration and junction

cad.pattern: Four-sided flashing set around linear wall opening
cad.placement: At cladding opening around waling plate
cad.end: Outside face below and beside waling plate
cad.opening: Waling plate and fasteners pass through the flashed cladding opening
cad.load: Water-shedding components fixed to wall framing and waling plate

notes: The flashing arrangement must suit the actual framing and cladding; a generic cap over the plate does not weather the lower and side edges.

objects.name: waling-plate top flashing
objects.definition: A flashing over the upper edge of the waling plate junction that receives water from behind or on the cladding and turns it out over the external face.
functions: Protect the top of the waling plate
Bridge the opened cladding junction
Discharge water to the exterior

cad.pattern: Continuous folded or flexible run over waling plate
cad.placement: At top edge of wall opening
cad.opening: Returns around fasteners or connectors are detailed
cad.load: Self-weight and water to wall framing and waling plate fixings

objects.name: waling-plate bottom flashing
objects.definition: A flashing below the waling plate junction that collects water from the opened wall interface and drains it to the outside face of the wall or cladding.
functions: Collect water below the junction
Protect the lower cladding cut edge
Discharge water clear of the wall

cad.pattern: Continuous tray or folded run below waling plate
cad.placement: At bottom edge of wall opening
cad.start: Behind junction and lower cladding edge
cad.opening: Drained cavity path remains open
cad.load: Self-weight and water to framing or cladding support

objects.name: waling-plate side flashing
objects.definition: A vertical flashing return at either end of a waling-plate wall opening that protects the cut cladding edge and directs water toward the lower flashing.
functions: Close the side of the cladding opening
Protect wall framing and cut edges
Direct side-entry water to the exterior drainage path

cad.pattern: Paired vertical flashing returns
cad.placement: At each end of waling-plate cladding opening
cad.opening: Bounds the wall opening beside the plate
cad.load: Self-weight and water to framing fixings

objects.name: waling-flashing lap sealant
objects.definition: A compatible sealant bead installed between overlapping lengths of waling-junction flashing before the lap is fixed.
functions: Limit water tracking through the flashing lap
Fill small irregularities between lap faces
Work with the overlap and mechanical fixings

cad.pattern: Continuous bead between flashing lap faces
cad.placement: Within each flashing overlap
cad.opening: Does not block intended drainage outlets
cad.load: Sealing role only; overlap fixings retain the lap

notes: Sealant supplements the correctly oriented lap and fasteners; it is not a substitute for them.

objects.name: deck or balcony diagonal strap-bracing assembly
objects.definition: A pair or set of diagonally opposed steel straps fixed across the joists and connected to the waling plate to brace an attached deck or balcony in plan.
functions: Restrain plan racking
Tie the deck framing back to the wall attachment line
Distribute in-plane actions across multiple joists

ncc_references.relationship: Requires the prescribed diagonal steel strap arrangement for the eligible attached deck or balcony.

cad.pattern: Opposed diagonal runs crossing repeated joists
cad.placement: Across top or underside of deck or balcony joists
cad.opening: Routes around openings and services only where the structural detail permits
cad.load: In-plane racking forces through strap tension to joists and waling plate

notes: Longer projections may require a secondary strap set; projection and required arrangement remain constraints.

objects.name: galvanized deck diagonal bracing strap
objects.definition: A thin galvanized steel strip run diagonally across a series of deck or balcony joists as the tension element in the plan-bracing assembly.
functions: Act as a diagonal tension tie
Connect successive joists into the bracing path
Tie the braced deck plane to the waling plate

cad.pattern: Continuous diagonal strip crossing each joist
cad.placement: On top or underside of deck framing
cad.opening: Fastener holes occur at each nominated framing crossing
cad.load: Axial tension between fixed intersections

notes: Its nominated width and thickness are connection attributes, not a generic material-library assumption.

objects.name: deck bracing-strap fixing
objects.definition: A corrosion-compatible nail or screw installed through the diagonal bracing strap into each nominated joist and into the waling plate.
functions: Connect the strap to each framing member
Transfer strap tension into joists and waling plate
Hold the strap in its designed route

cad.pattern: Repeated at every nominated strap-to-framing intersection
cad.placement: Through strap into joist or waling plate
cad.end: Embedment in timber or detailed steel connection
cad.opening: Passes through strap hole or punched location
cad.load: Local shear transfers strap force to framing

notes: Fastener count, type and substrate must follow the selected detail; a rendered dot is not adequate fabrication information.

objects.name: residential swimming-pool physical system
objects.definition: The water-retaining pool or spa construction, surrounding access barrier and water-recirculation equipment treated as connected but independently checkable physical systems.
functions: Contain bathing water
Restrict unsupervised young-child access
Circulate and treat water without dangerous suction exposure

ncc_references.relationship: Provides the national Deemed-to-Satisfy references for eligible pool barriers and water-recirculation safety, subject to jurisdiction variations.

cad.pattern: Pool vessel with perimeter barrier and connected plant network
cad.placement: At the dwelling site or within an associated enclosure
cad.end: Finished waterline, barrier and operating equipment
cad.opening: Pool interior, gates, suction outlets and service penetrations remain explicit
cad.load: Water, earth, occupant and environmental actions to shell and site; hydraulic actions to plant

notes: Queensland, Northern Territory, New South Wales, South Australia and Tasmania have material variations or local legislation. A national template must expose jurisdiction rather than hide it.

objects.name: in-ground swimming-pool assembly
objects.definition: A swimming-pool vessel installed substantially below surrounding ground, including its shell, prepared support, backfill or earth interface, coping edge, interior finish and shell penetrations.
functions: Contain swimming water below ground level
Transfer water and ground actions
Provide a finished perimeter and interfaces for pool fittings

cad.pattern: Excavated vessel with perimeter shell and layered support
cad.placement: Below finished ground or pool-surround level
cad.opening: Open top and shell penetrations are explicit
cad.load: Water pressure, earth pressure, groundwater and use actions to shell and ground

notes: The shell still needs structural design under the NCC; the pool-safety standards do not replace that design.

objects.name: reinforced-concrete pool shell assembly
objects.definition: A site-formed reinforced-concrete pool floor and walls acting together as the structural water-retaining shell, with construction joints, penetrations and applied interior finish.
functions: Resist water and ground actions
Form the pool geometry
Provide a stable substrate for waterproof interior finishes and fittings

cad.pattern: Monolithic or jointed reinforced floor-and-wall shell
cad.placement: Within pool excavation
cad.opening: Fitting penetrations, overflow and construction joints remain explicit
cad.load: Hydrostatic and earth actions through reinforced shell to ground

notes: Shotcrete, sprayed concrete and conventionally placed concrete are construction choices, not assumed synonyms for every concrete shell.

objects.name: prefabricated fibreglass pool shell assembly
objects.definition: A factory-moulded composite pool shell placed into a prepared excavation and supported by its base, controlled backfill, plumbing interfaces and perimeter bond or coping construction.
functions: Provide the structural and watertight pool vessel
Form integrated steps, benches and waterline geometry
Connect factory openings to site plumbing

cad.pattern: Product-specific moulded vessel in excavation
cad.placement: On prepared pool base with backfill around shell
cad.opening: Factory or site-cut fitting openings are explicit
cad.load: Water and ground actions through composite shell to bedding and backfill

notes: Shell dimensions and installation layers must come from the selected manufacturer and site engineering.

objects.name: above-ground swimming-pool assembly
objects.definition: A pool vessel standing wholly or partly above surrounding ground, commonly formed by a supported wall, liner, top rail, base track and external support or deck interfaces.
functions: Contain swimming water above ground
Transfer water pressure through wall and support frame
Provide interfaces for recirculation fittings and access
not_synonyms: pool wall as compliant barrier automatically

cad.pattern: Raised circular, oval or rectangular vessel with repeated supports
cad.placement: On prepared ground or structural platform
cad.opening: Open top and wall fitting openings are explicit
cad.load: Water pressure through liner and wall to base and supports

notes: Some jurisdictions do not accept an above-ground pool wall as the access barrier. Barrier role must be checked explicitly.

objects.name: residential spa-pool assembly
objects.definition: A compact pool or manufactured spa vessel intended for sitting or reclining bathing, including its shell, support base, circulation fittings, equipment enclosure and selected access-control barrier or secure cover.
functions: Contain heated bathing water
Support seats and hydrotherapy fittings
Coordinate child-access restriction and recirculation safety

cad.pattern: Compact moulded vessel with perimeter cabinet or buried shell
cad.placement: On structural base, deck or in prepared excavation
cad.opening: Open water surface, access cover and service panels are explicit
cad.load: Filled vessel and occupants to support; hydraulic loads to equipment

notes: A spa is included in the NCC swimming-pool definition, but local rules can provide different access-control options.

objects.name: pool excavation
objects.definition: The formed ground void cut to receive an in-ground pool shell, prepared base, plumbing clearances, backfill and groundwater-management provisions.
functions: Provide space for the pool shell and construction layers
Establish founding levels and working clearance
Expose the ground conditions requiring support or groundwater control

cad.pattern: Subtracted ground volume following pool profile with construction allowance
cad.placement: At designed pool position
cad.opening: The entire cut is an opening in the ground model
cad.load: Ground boundary only; temporary stability requires separate design

notes: Excavation geometry is drawable, but safe excavation, shoring and groundwater management are separate temporary-works decisions.

objects.name: pool shell prepared base
objects.definition: A levelled and shaped layer of specified bedding or structural support placed at the bottom of the pool excavation to receive the shell.
functions: Provide continuous shell support
Establish level and designed floor profile
Separate the shell from irregular excavation material

cad.pattern: Continuous shaped layer below shell
cad.placement: On excavation base
cad.opening: Drainage or relief points remain explicit
cad.load: Shell and water loads distributed to founding ground

notes: Material and compaction are selected-system and geotechnical inputs, not universal defaults.

objects.name: pool shell side backfill
objects.definition: Selected material placed and controlled between an in-ground pool shell and the excavation side to support the shell and fill the construction annulus.
functions: Support the outside of the shell
Transfer shell actions to surrounding ground
Protect and embed external pool plumbing where permitted

cad.pattern: Annular fill volume around pool shell
cad.placement: Between shell exterior and excavation face
cad.opening: Plumbing routes and groundwater points remain coordinated
cad.load: Shell lateral actions to ground and ground actions back to shell

notes: Wrong backfill or uncoordinated filling can deform a proprietary shell; follow the selected installation system.

objects.name: pool perimeter bond beam
objects.definition: A reinforced concrete perimeter member around the top of a pool shell that stiffens and ties the edge and supports coping or adjoining pavement where designed.
functions: Stiffen the pool perimeter
Tie shell edge and surrounding construction
Support coping and edge finishes

cad.pattern: Continuous or jointed ring around pool perimeter
cad.placement: At top edge of in-ground shell
cad.start: Closed perimeter start or construction joint
cad.opening: Skimmer throats and other edge fittings interrupt or pass through locally
cad.load: Perimeter and coping loads to shell and ground

notes: The term is common, but its structural relationship differs between concrete and proprietary fibreglass pool systems.

objects.name: pool coping
objects.definition: The finished cap or edge unit around the pool perimeter that covers the shell or bond-beam edge and forms the transition to the surrounding surface.
functions: Provide a durable pool edge
Cover and protect the shell perimeter
Form a comfortable and drainable transition to the surround

cad.pattern: Repeated units or continuous cap around pool edge
cad.placement: On shell lip or perimeter bond beam
cad.opening: Skimmer lids and fittings interrupt the run
cad.load: Foot traffic and edge loads to bond beam or shell support

notes: Coping is not automatically the child-access barrier and does not define the non-climbable zone.

objects.name: pool interior finish
objects.definition: The exposed water-contact finish applied to or formed as part of the pool shell, such as aggregate render, tile, vinyl liner or composite gelcoat.
functions: Provide the finished water-contact surface
Protect or complete the shell system
Form colour, texture and cleanable geometry

cad.pattern: Continuous inner-surface layer following shell geometry
cad.placement: On inner face of pool shell
cad.opening: Wrapped or sealed around every pool fitting
cad.load: Finish adhesion and water exposure to shell substrate

notes: Gelcoat is integral to many fibreglass shells, while tile or render is a separately installed finish; keep construction method explicit.

objects.name: pool perimeter isolation joint
objects.definition: A movement joint separating pool coping or shell-edge construction from adjoining paving or another rigid surround, filled with compatible backing and sealant where required.
functions: Allow differential movement
Limit rigid load transfer into the shell edge
Seal the exposed gap while preserving movement

cad.pattern: Continuous gap and seal around pool perimeter
cad.placement: Between coping or bond beam and adjoining rigid paving
cad.start: Closed perimeter start or joint intersection
cad.opening: Joint gap is retained as geometry beneath sealant
cad.load: Movement accommodation rather than structural load transfer

notes: Calling every perimeter joint an expansion joint can hide whether it isolates, controls shrinkage or joins pours; retain the designed joint role.

objects.name: pool hydrostatic-relief assembly
objects.definition: A valve, drain point or standpipe arrangement intended to relieve or monitor groundwater pressure beneath or around an in-ground pool shell.
functions: Reduce damaging uplift pressure when the pool water level is low
Provide groundwater observation or pumping access
Connect sub-shell drainage to a maintainable point

cad.pattern: Local valve or pipe route from below shell to accessible point
cad.placement: At deepest shell region or outside shell as designed
cad.end: Valve, standpipe or accessible pump point
cad.opening: Shell or surround access opening remains explicit
cad.load: Hydraulic pressure-relief role only

notes: Groundwater control is site- and system-specific. A hydrostatic valve does not remove the need for structural and installation design.

objects.name: above-ground pool wall
objects.definition: The continuous or segmented vertical wall that contains and supports the liner and water pressure in an above-ground pool system.
functions: Resist outward water pressure
Support the liner perimeter
Connect top rail, base track and uprights

cad.pattern: Continuous curved wall or repeated panel ring
cad.placement: Around above-ground pool liner
cad.opening: Skimmer and return openings are explicit
cad.load: Water pressure through liner to wall, uprights and base

notes: Do not infer barrier compliance from wall height or appearance; local rules and the full access context control.

objects.name: above-ground pool liner
objects.definition: A flexible watertight membrane fitted inside an above-ground pool wall and floor, shaped and restrained at the top edge and sealed around fittings.
functions: Contain pool water
Protect the structural wall from direct water contact
Form the exposed inner pool surface
not_synonyms: waterproofing of a concrete shell automatically

cad.pattern: Flexible inner skin following wall and floor
cad.placement: Inside above-ground pool structure
cad.opening: Gasketed fitting penetrations remain explicit
cad.load: Water pressure carried through liner to supporting wall and base

objects.name: above-ground pool top rail
objects.definition: A continuous or segmented horizontal cap member around an above-ground pool that ties wall uprights, covers the wall edge and retains or protects the liner connection.
functions: Tie and stiffen the top of the pool wall
Cover the wall and liner edge
Connect repeated upright supports

cad.pattern: Repeated horizontal segments forming closed perimeter
cad.placement: At top of above-ground pool wall
cad.opening: Interrupts at skimmer or access features only as designed
cad.load: Wall-edge stiffening to uprights; not assumed as an occupant support

objects.name: spa-pool secure cover assembly
objects.definition: A rigid or reinforced cover, attachment points and locking devices designed to close a spa-pool opening as an access-control option only where the applicable jurisdiction permits it.
functions: Close the spa water opening
Resist removal by young children
Reduce heat loss and debris entry as secondary functions

cad.pattern: Folding or removable rigid panels spanning spa opening
cad.placement: Across spa-pool top lip
cad.start: Fixed hinge or first attachment edge
cad.opening: Open, folded and secured closed states are separate
cad.load: Cover loads to spa rim and strap anchors

notes: Whether a cover can replace a barrier is a jurisdiction-specific legal question. The object must never be offered as a universal national alternative.

objects.name: swimming-pool safety barrier system
objects.definition: The continuous physical barrier around the pool hazard, including fence or wall segments, gates, permitted opening treatments, posts, panels, fixings and ground or structure interfaces.
functions: Restrict access by young children
Remain continuous around the nominated hazard
Self-close and self-latch at access gates

ncc_references.relationship: Requires a continuous barrier and points eligible construction to the applicable AS 1926 barrier publications, subject to jurisdiction variations.

cad.pattern: Closed barrier route made from segments and controlled openings
cad.placement: Between pool hazard and unsupervised approach routes
cad.opening: Every gate, door, window or gap is a modelled opening with treatment
cad.load: Barrier and impact actions through panels, posts and anchors to substrate

notes: Barrier height, gaps, climbable features and clear zones are constraints derived from the adopted rules; they are not invisible extra solids.

objects.name: pool isolation-fence assembly
objects.definition: A fence and gate arrangement separating the pool and its immediate surrounds from the dwelling and the rest of the property rather than relying on the property boundary alone.
functions: Isolate the pool hazard from normal property circulation
Provide controlled gate access
Complete a continuous child-resistant barrier route

cad.pattern: Closed or building-returned fence route
cad.placement: Around pool and immediate pool surrounds
cad.opening: Only scheduled controlled gates or treated openings interrupt the route
cad.load: Fence actions to posts, spigots and support substrate

notes: The immediate-pool-surround extent is a regulatory and project decision, not a standard object width.

objects.name: pool boundary-barrier assembly
objects.definition: A property-boundary fence or wall segment intentionally used as part of the swimming-pool barrier and assessed from both the pool side and the adjoining side under the applicable rules.
functions: Complete the pool barrier at the property boundary
Resist access from adjoining land
Coordinate boundary construction with pool-side clear zones

cad.pattern: Linear boundary segment forming part of closed pool-barrier route
cad.placement: On or near property boundary beside pool area
cad.opening: Gaps and any boundary gate remain explicit
cad.load: Fence or wall actions to footings and ground

notes: Changes made by a neighbour can affect the barrier. Record both faces and do not assume the title boundary itself is a physical barrier.

objects.name: aluminium tubular pool-fence assembly
objects.definition: A proprietary fence system made from aluminium panels, posts, brackets, caps, base plates, fixings and gates configured for swimming-pool access restriction.
functions: Form a lightweight open pool barrier
Transfer panel loads through posts to substrate
Provide compatible gate and corner construction

cad.pattern: Repeated prefabricated panels between posts
cad.placement: Along scheduled pool-barrier route
cad.end: End post, corner or gate post
cad.opening: Picket gaps and gate openings are actual geometry
cad.load: Panel and impact actions through brackets and posts to substrate

notes: A visually similar garden panel is not assumed to have pool-barrier evidence.

objects.name: aluminium tubular pool-fence panel
objects.definition: A prefabricated aluminium panel with horizontal rails and repeated vertical pickets fitted between pool-fence posts.
functions: Fill the barrier span between posts
Restrict passage through the fence
Transfer impact and wind loads to panel brackets and posts
materials: welded powder-coated aluminium extrusions or tubes

cad.pattern: Repeated vertical pickets between top and bottom rails
cad.placement: Between pool-fence posts
cad.opening: Picket and ground gaps are explicit
cad.load: Panel actions to rail brackets and posts

objects.name: pool-fence post
objects.definition: A vertical post supporting pool-fence panels, corners or gates and transferring their actions into a footing, base plate or structural substrate.
functions: Support barrier panels and hardware
Maintain barrier alignment and height
Transfer loads to the substrate
materials: timber or masonry where a designed system uses them
attributes: line corner end or gate post

cad.pattern: Repeated at panel ends, corners and gate sides
cad.placement: Along pool-barrier route
cad.opening: Defines panel and gate openings between adjacent posts
cad.load: Barrier, gate and wind actions to footing or substrate

notes: Gate posts can require different section, footing or reinforcement from ordinary line posts.

objects.name: pool-fence post cap
objects.definition: A fitted cap closing the open top of a hollow pool-fence post and completing its weather and injury-resistant finish.
functions: Close the post opening
Shed water from the post top

Keep the stored cover clear of circulation paths where placed correctly

objects.name: integrated pool entry-step assembly

Coordinate handholds, finishes and shell structure

objects.name: pool access ladder assembly

Transfer occupant loads to anchors
Allow removal or closure where required by the access-control strategy

objects.name: pool entry handrail

Provide a graspable support
Transfer user loads to deck or shell anchors

objects.name: domestic solid-fuel heating system
objects.definition: A complete domestic solid-fuel appliance or open fireplace with its hearth, heat protection, chimney or flue system, termination and building penetrations.

Contain fire and hot combustion products
Discharge smoke above the building without overheating nearby construction

objects.name: open masonry fireplace assembly
objects.definition: A site-built open fireplace with non-combustible hearth, masonry firebox, opening support, throat, smoke chamber and masonry chimney carrying combustion products above the roof.

Radiate heat into the room
Collect and discharge smoke through the chimney

objects.name: open-fireplace front hearth

Extend the fireplace base into the room

objects.name: open-fireplace back hearth
objects.definition: The non-combustible floor of the masonry firebox behind the opening, built to support burning fuel and withstand direct heat.

Protect supporting construction from direct fire
Form the lower firebox surface

cad.pattern: Refractory floor within firebox

cad.opening: Ash-dump opening remains explicit where used
cad.load: Fuel and firebox loads to masonry support

objects.name: masonry fireplace firebox assembly
objects.definition: The refractory floor, back wall and side walls enclosing the fuel and flame zone of an open masonry fireplace below the throat.

Reflect heat toward the room
Guide combustion products toward the throat

cad.pattern: Three-sided refractory enclosure with open front

cad.opening: Front firebox mouth remains fully open

objects.name: fireplace inner masonry leaf
objects.definition: The inner solid-masonry construction immediately outside or supporting the refractory firebox and lower smoke path.

Support firebox and smoke-chamber geometry
Separate hot inner construction from the outer leaf or building

cad.pattern: Masonry envelope following firebox and smoke chamber
cad.placement: Outside refractory inner face
cad.opening: Firebox mouth and flue passage remain open
cad.load: Masonry loads to hearth and foundation

objects.name: fireplace outer masonry leaf
objects.definition: The outer masonry enclosure around an open fireplace and chimney base, separated from hotter inner construction by the designed cavity or thickness.

Protect adjacent building construction
Support finishes and chimney mass where designed

cad.pattern: Outer masonry envelope around fireplace core

objects.name: fireplace masonry separation cavity
objects.definition: The continuous physical air space between inner and outer fireplace masonry where the selected construction uses separated leaves.

Keep the masonry leaves physically separated
Provide the designed thermal and construction break

cad.pattern: Continuous void between masonry leaves
cad.placement: Around firebox, smoke chamber or chimney base as detailed
cad.opening: Penetrations and closures remain explicit
cad.load: No structural load; geometry controls separation

objects.name: fireplace opening lintel
objects.definition: A non-combustible horizontal member or formed arch supporting masonry above the open fireplace mouth.
functions: Bridge the firebox opening
Support masonry above
Maintain the designed fireplace throat and opening geometry

cad.pattern: Single member or voussoir arch over opening
cad.placement: At top of fireplace mouth
cad.opening: Spans the open firebox mouth
cad.load: Masonry above to side bearings

objects.name: fireplace throat
objects.definition: The narrowed passage above the firebox opening where combustion products enter the smoke chamber and where a damper may be installed.
functions: Accelerate and guide smoke into the chimney path
Separate firebox from smoke chamber geometry
Receive a compatible flue damper where fitted

cad.pattern: Narrow slot-like passage above firebox
cad.placement: Between firebox and smoke chamber
cad.opening: Continuous gas passage remains open
cad.load: No structural load; bounded by supported masonry

objects.name: fireplace smoke chamber
objects.definition: The tapered enclosed volume above a fireplace throat that gathers smoke from the broad firebox opening and transitions it into the narrower chimney flue.
functions: Collect combustion products
Smooth the change from firebox width to flue size
Direct smoke upward with limited turbulence

cad.pattern: Tapered enclosed volume from throat to flue
cad.placement: Above fireplace opening within masonry enclosure
cad.opening: Internal gas volume remains continuous
cad.load: Masonry enclosure loads to fireplace support

notes: The volume is modelled because its geometry materially affects the assembly; smoke itself is not an object.

objects.name: masonry chimney assembly
objects.definition: A vertical masonry shaft containing one or more combustion-product passages, with liners or parging, structural support, roof penetration, crown and termination components.
functions: Enclose the flue passage
Carry combustion products above the roof
Protect nearby building elements from heat and weather
materials: clay or metal liner where selected

cad.pattern: Vertical masonry shaft through building and roof
cad.placement: Above masonry fireplace or connected appliance
cad.opening: Continuous flue passage and cleanout remain explicit
cad.load: Masonry self-weight to foundation; wind and seismic actions through shaft

objects.name: masonry chimney flue passage
objects.definition: The continuous internal passage within a masonry chimney through which smoke and hot combustion products travel to the outside.
functions: Carry combustion products
Maintain a contained draft path
Connect the smoke chamber or appliance to the termination

cad.pattern: Continuous enclosed vertical gas path
cad.placement: Inside masonry chimney shaft
cad.opening: Bore remains continuous and unobstructed
cad.load: Hot-gas containment rather than structural load

objects.name: masonry chimney crown
objects.definition: A weather-shedding slab or rendered cap at the top of a masonry chimney shaft around the flue outlet.

Protect exposed masonry cores and joints
Form a durable transition to flue liner or cap

cad.pattern: Sloped cap around flue outlet
cad.placement: At top of masonry chimney
cad.opening: Flue passage remains open through crown
cad.load: Self-weight and weather actions to chimney shaft

objects.name: freestanding wood-heater assembly
objects.definition: A factory-made solid-fuel room heater standing on legs or a pedestal and connected through a flue collar to a tested flue system, with a floor protector and wall shielding where required.
functions: Burn wood in a controlled firebox
Transfer heat to the room
Connect safely to a flue system

cad.pattern: Packaged appliance on hearth with top or rear flue connection
cad.placement: Inside room at tested clearance from surrounding construction
cad.opening: Door swing, firebox and air inlets remain explicit
cad.load: Appliance mass to floor protector and floor; flue reaction to collar and supports

notes: Use the selected appliance's certified installation instructions; similar-looking heaters can require different clearances and floor protection.

objects.name: wood-heater body and firebox
objects.definition: The welded or cast outer body and enclosed combustion chamber of a freestanding wood heater, including its top, sides, back and flue outlet structure.
functions: Contain the controlled fire
Transfer heat through designed surfaces
Support door, lining, baffle and flue collar

cad.pattern: Closed metal box or shaped casting around firebox
cad.placement: On heater pedestal or legs
cad.opening: Door and air openings remain explicit
cad.load: Firebox, fuel and component loads to base

objects.name: wood-heater firebox door assembly
objects.definition: A hinged high-temperature door with metal frame, ceramic glass or solid panel, perimeter gasket, handle and latch closing the wood-heater firebox opening.
functions: Close and seal the firebox
Allow fuel loading and ash access
Provide a controlled viewing opening where glazed

cad.pattern: Single hinged panel at firebox front
cad.placement: At wood-heater loading opening
cad.opening: Door opening and swing envelope are explicit
cad.load: Door mass and seal compression to heater body

objects.name: wood-heater ceramic door glass
objects.definition: A high-temperature transparent ceramic panel retained and gasketed in a wood-heater door to allow a view of the fire while containing combustion.
functions: Close the viewing opening
Withstand high thermal exposure
Transmit radiant heat and visible light

cad.pattern: Single transparent panel in door aperture
cad.placement: Within wood-heater door frame

cad.load: Thermal and pressure actions to door retainers

objects.name: wood-heater door latch
objects.definition: A handle-operated cam, hook or catch that pulls the wood-heater door against its perimeter gasket and holds it closed.

Compress the door gasket
Provide controlled hot-door operation

cad.pattern: Single operating mechanism at door edge
cad.placement: Opposite wood-heater door hinges
cad.opening: Moves clear for door opening

objects.name: wood-heater internal baffle
objects.definition: A refractory or steel plate near the top of a wood-heater firebox that lengthens the combustion-gas path before gases enter the flue outlet.

Support secondary combustion and heat transfer
Shield the top of the firebox from direct flame

cad.pattern: Single or multiple plates below firebox roof

cad.opening: Leaves product-specific gas passage to flue
cad.load: Self-weight and thermal action to internal supports

objects.name: wood-heater firebrick lining

Provide a durable fuel-contact lining

objects.name: wood-heater grate and ash-pan assembly

Provide removable ash collection

objects.name: wood-heater combustion-air control
objects.definition: A lever, slider or rotary damper controlling the amount and route of combustion air entering a wood-heater firebox.

Distribute primary, secondary or airwash flow
Provide a user-operable burn control

cad.opening: Changes effective combustion-air opening

Maintain the underside air and cleaning space

objects.name: wood-heater floor protector

Provide a durable level appliance base

cad.opening: Continuous beneath appliance except designed anchors
cad.load: Appliance and use loads to floor structure

objects.name: ventilated wood-heater wall-shield assembly
objects.definition: A non-combustible sheet mounted on spacers in front of an adjacent wall with open lower and upper edges that allow air to circulate behind the shield.

Create a ventilated cooling path
Allow a tested or prescribed appliance location where the selected path permits

objects.name: wood-heater wall-shield sheet
objects.definition: The non-combustible planar face of a ventilated wall shield positioned between a wood heater and adjacent wall construction.

Form the outer face of the ventilated shield
Transfer its own weight to spacer fixings

Support the shield sheet
Transfer shield loads without filling the air space

cad.opening: Occupies only local points in ventilated cavity
cad.load: Shield weight and local actions to wall

objects.name: solid-fuel fireplace-insert assembly

Transfer heat to the room
Connect the appliance outlet to the full chimney or flue path

objects.name: domestic solid-fuel flue system
objects.definition: A tested system of active inner flue, surrounding casings or insulation, joints, supports, ceiling and roof penetration components, storm collar and terminal cowl carrying combustion products from an appliance outdoors.

Maintain required separation from building materials
Remain supported and weathered through the building and roof

objects.name: solid-fuel active inner flue pipe

Maintain the designed draft bore
Connect appliance outlet to terminal without leakage

objects.name: solid-fuel flue intermediate casing

objects.name: solid-fuel flue outer casing
objects.definition: The outermost concentric metal casing of a solid-fuel flue system, defining the tested external boundary through ceiling and roof construction.

Protect the internal flue layers
Provide the outer surface coordinated with penetration clearances and supports

Maintain gas containment and casing continuity

objects.name: solid-fuel flue joint clamp

Transfer local axial and lateral actions

objects.name: solid-fuel flue support bracket

Restrain lateral movement and offsets
Transfer wind and installation actions to building structure

Maintain the tested flue and ventilation geometry

objects.name: bushfire gutter ember-guard assembly

objects.name: bushfire subfloor enclosure assembly

objects.name: bushfire subfloor mesh screen

objects.name: bushfire window-screen assembly

objects.name: bushfire screen-door assembly

objects.name: bushfire shutter assembly

objects.name: bushfire opening-perimeter seal

objects.name: bushfire external-door bottom seal

objects.name: bushfire service-penetration closure

objects.name: above-ground private bushfire shelter

waterproofing and earth cover where buried
